steps.title: I need…
steps.how_to: How to say what you need and what you have to do at an office.
steps.intro: At an Italian office you'll hear bisogna for what you have to do and serve or servono for what you need. You can use them yourself to ask what to bring.

examples.said: Bisogna prendere il numero.
examples.en: You have to take a ticket.

examples.said: Serve una marca da bollo da sedici euro.
examples.en: You need a sixteen-euro revenue stamp.

examples.said: Servono due fototessere.
examples.en: You need two passport photos.

examples.said: Bisogna prendere l'appuntamento online?
examples.en: Do you have to book the appointment online?

steps.notice: Bisogna is followed by a verb and never changes; serve and servono are followed by the thing you need, servono for more than one, because the thing is what's needed.
steps.context: Italian offices often want an appointment booked online and a marca da bollo bought beforehand at a tabaccheria.

ask.said: Sei all'anagrafe e c'è la fila. Cosa fai prima?
ask.en: You're at the registry office and there's a line. What do you do first?

answer.said: Prima bisogna prendere il numero.
answer.en: First you have to take a ticket.

ask.said: Cosa porti in comune per la residenza?
ask.en: What do you bring to city hall to register your residence?

answer.said: Servono il passaporto e il contratto d'affitto.
answer.en: You need your passport and your lease.

ask.said: Per il permesso di soggiorno, cosa porti in questura?
ask.en: For your residence permit, what do you bring to the police headquarters?

answer.said: Servono la ricevuta e quattro fototessere.
answer.en: You need the receipt and four passport photos.

mission.goal: Ask what you need to register your residence.

say.said: Buongiorno, devo richiedere la residenza. Cosa serve?
say.en: Good morning, I need to register my residence. What do I need?

steps.title: How much?
steps.how_to: How to check what's enough and how long it takes, with basta and ci vuole.
steps.intro: Basta tells you something is enough, and ci vuole tells you what something takes, like time. Together they let you check with a clerk what to bring and how long you'll wait.

examples.said: Per il contratto basta la fotocopia?
examples.en: For the lease, is a photocopy enough?

examples.said: Sì, basta la fotocopia, e bastano due fototessere.
examples.en: Yes, a photocopy is enough, and two passport photos are enough.

examples.said: Quanto tempo ci vuole?
examples.en: How long does it take?

examples.said: Ci vogliono alcune settimane.
examples.en: It takes a few weeks.

steps.notice: Basta says something is enough and ci vuole says what it takes; both turn plural, bastano and ci vogliono, when what follows is plural.
steps.context: Italian offices usually ask for the original and a photocopy of every document.

ask.said: Hai solo la fotocopia del contratto. Cosa chiedi all'impiegata?
ask.en: You only have a photocopy of your lease. What do you ask the clerk?

answer.said: Mi scusi, basta una fotocopia?
answer.en: Excuse me, is a copy enough?

ask.said: Il tuo amico vuole portare dieci fototessere. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: Your friend wants to bring ten passport photos. What do you tell him?

answer.said: Bastano quattro fototessere.
answer.en: Four passport photos are enough.

ask.said: Per la residenza, quanto aspetti di solito?
ask.en: For residence registration, how long do you usually wait?

answer.said: Di solito ci vogliono quarantacinque giorni.
answer.en: It usually takes forty-five days.

mission.goal: Ask whether a photocopy of your lease is enough.

say.said: Per il contratto basta la fotocopia?
say.en: For the lease, is a photocopy enough?

steps.title: Instructions
steps.how_to: How to understand the polite instructions a clerk gives you.
steps.intro: Clerks give instructions with the polite command form. Once you know the endings, you can follow them without asking for English.

examples.said: Compili il modulo.
examples.en: Fill out the form.

examples.said: Firmi qui in fondo.
examples.en: Sign here at the bottom.

examples.said: Prenda il numero e aspetti.
examples.en: Take a ticket and wait.

examples.said: Torni con la ricevuta fra trenta giorni.
examples.en: Come back with the receipt in thirty days.

steps.notice: A polite instruction ends in -i for -are verbs and in -a for -ere and -ire verbs, so firmi means "sign," not "you sign."

ask.said: L'impiegata dice: "Compili il modulo e firmi qui." Cosa fai?
ask.en: The clerk says, "Fill out the form and sign here." What do you do?

answer.said: Compilo il modulo e poi lo firmo.
answer.en: I fill out the form and then sign it.

ask.said: All'anagrafe l'impiegato dice: "Prenda il numero e aspetti." Cosa fai?
ask.en: At the registry office the clerk says, "Take a ticket and wait." What do you do?

answer.said: Prendo il numero e aspetto il mio turno.
answer.en: I take a ticket and wait my turn.

ask.said: L'impiegato dice: "Torni con la ricevuta fra trenta giorni." Cosa fai?
ask.en: The clerk says, "Come back with the receipt in thirty days." What do you do?

answer.said: Tengo la ricevuta e torno fra un mese.
answer.en: I hang on to the receipt and come back in a month.

mission.goal: Ask the clerk what to do next and follow the instructions.

say.said: Mi scusi, cosa devo fare adesso?
say.en: Excuse me, what do I do now?

steps.title: How come?
steps.how_to: How to ask which one, how come, and how much or how long.
steps.intro: Quale, come mai and quanto let you ask for exactly what you need, at an office counter or when you meet someone new. Each one asks for something different.

examples.said: Quale modulo devo compilare?
examples.en: Which form do I need to fill out?

examples.said: Quali sono le Sue difficoltà con l'italiano?
examples.en: What do you struggle with in Italian?

examples.said: Come mai proprio in Italia?
examples.en: Why Italy, of all places?

examples.said: Quanto dura il corso e quanto costa?
examples.en: How long is the course, and how much does it cost?

steps.notice: Quale asks which one and quali which ones, because it agrees; come mai asks how come, and quanto asks how much or how long, as in quanto costa and quanto dura.

ask.said: Ci sono tre moduli sul tavolo. Cosa chiedi?
ask.en: There are three forms on the table. What do you ask?

answer.said: Scusi, quale devo compilare?
answer.en: Excuse me, which one do I fill out?

ask.said: Al telefono ti dicono che manca un documento. Come rispondi?
ask.en: On the phone they tell you a document is missing. How do you answer?

answer.said: Come mai? L'ho consegnato a maggio!
answer.en: How come? I turned it in in May!

ask.said: Vuoi iscriverti a un corso d'italiano. Cosa chiedi alla scuola?
ask.en: You want to sign up for an Italian course. What do you ask the school?

answer.said: Quanto costa il corso al mese?
answer.en: How much is the course per month?

mission.goal: At a language school, ask how long the course lasts and what it costs.

say.said: Quanto dura il corso e quanto costa?
say.en: How long is the course, and how much does it cost?

steps.title: Describe it
steps.how_to: How to say which person or thing you mean by describing it with che.
steps.intro: Che joins two ideas, as in "the bank my landlady recommended." You'll use it to say exactly which account, apartment or person you mean.

examples.said: È la banca che mi ha consigliato la padrona di casa.
examples.en: It's the bank my landlady recommended.

examples.said: Allora, prendi il bilocale che abbiamo visto ieri?
examples.en: So, are you taking the one-bedroom we saw yesterday?

examples.said: L'idraulico che chiamo di solito è in ferie.
examples.en: The plumber I usually call is on vacation.

examples.said: Il conto che ho aperto è gratuito.
examples.en: The account I opened is free.

steps.notice: Che links a person or thing to what you say about it, whether it does the action or receives it; Italian always says che, even where English drops "that."

ask.said: Quale appartamento ti piace di più?
ask.en: Which apartment do you like best?

answer.said: Mi piace il bilocale che abbiamo visto ieri.
answer.en: I like the one-bedroom we saw yesterday.

ask.said: Il bancomat ti ha mangiato la carta. Quale carta era?
ask.en: The ATM ate your card. Which card was it?

answer.said: Quella che mi ha dato la banca la settimana scorsa.
answer.en: The one the bank gave me last week.

ask.said: Chi chiami se la caldaia è rotta?
ask.en: Who do you call if the boiler breaks?

answer.said: Chiamo l'idraulico che mi ha consigliato la padrona di casa.
answer.en: I call the plumber my landlady recommended.

mission.goal: Tell the clerk who recommended this bank.

say.said: È la banca che mi ha consigliato la padrona di casa.
say.en: It's the bank my landlady recommended.

steps.title: Which one?
steps.how_to: How to say which one you mean when a little word like con, di or in comes before it, with cui, or dove for a place.
steps.intro: Where English says "the person I talked to," Italian puts the little word first and then cui: la persona con cui ho parlato. For a place you can also say dove.

examples.said: La persona con cui ho parlato ieri oggi non c'è.
examples.en: The person I talked to yesterday isn't here today.

examples.said: Ecco, è questo il documento di cui ho bisogno.
examples.en: There, this is the document I need.

examples.said: La zona in cui vorrei vivere è vicino al mercato.
examples.en: The area I'd like to live in is near the market.

examples.said: Il bancomat lo ritira nella filiale dove ha aperto il conto.
examples.en: You pick up your debit card at the branch where you opened your account.

steps.notice: The little word comes first and cui follows, because an Italian sentence never ends on con, di or in; for a place, dove works too.

ask.said: Chi cerchi in banca?
ask.en: Who are you looking for at the bank?

answer.said: Cerco l'impiegata con cui ho parlato ieri.
answer.en: I'm looking for the clerk I talked to yesterday.

ask.said: Per aprire il conto, cosa chiedi all'impiegato?
ask.en: To open the account, what do you ask the clerk?

answer.said: Sono questi i documenti di cui ha bisogno?
answer.en: Are these the documents you need?

ask.said: In quale filiale ritiri la carta?
ask.en: Which branch do you pick up your card at?

answer.said: In quella in cui ho aperto il conto.
answer.en: At the one where I opened my account.

mission.goal: Ask for the clerk you talked to yesterday.

say.said: Cerco la persona con cui ho parlato ieri.
say.en: I'm looking for the person I talked to yesterday.

steps.title: What?
steps.how_to: How to say "what" meaning "the thing that" with quello che.
steps.intro: Quello che means "what" in the sense of "the thing that." You'll use it to say what you don't understand and what you were looking for.

examples.said: Non capisco bene quello che c'è scritto qui.
examples.en: I don't really understand what it says here.

examples.said: Mi dica pure quello che non è chiaro.
examples.en: Just tell me what isn't clear.

examples.said: È proprio quello che cercavo.
examples.en: It's just what I was looking for.

examples.said: Ciò che conta è la firma.
examples.en: What matters is the signature.

steps.notice: When "what" means "the thing that," Italian says quello che, or ciò che when it's more formal, because che alone can't stand for the thing.

ask.said: Il contratto è difficile. Cosa dici all'impiegato?
ask.en: The contract is hard to follow. What do you tell the clerk?

answer.said: Scusi, non capisco quello che c'è scritto nel contratto.
answer.en: Sorry, I don't understand what it says in the contract.

ask.said: Trovi il regalo perfetto per un'amica. Cosa dici?
ask.en: You find the perfect gift for a friend. What do you say?

answer.said: È proprio quello che le piace!
answer.en: It's just what she likes!

ask.said: In un conto corrente, cosa conta di più per te?
ask.en: In a checking account, what matters most to you?

answer.said: Quello che conta è il canone mensile.
answer.en: What matters is the monthly fee.

mission.goal: Tell the clerk which part of the contract you don't understand.

say.said: Non capisco bene quello che c'è scritto qui.
say.en: I don't really understand what it says here.

steps.title: Before!
steps.how_to: How to say before, with prima di when it's you and prima che when it's someone else.
steps.intro: Italian says "before" two ways: prima di plus a verb when you do both things, and prima che when the other action is someone else's. You'll use them at the bank and with friends.

examples.said: Prima di firmare, vorrei leggere le condizioni.
examples.en: Before I sign, I'd like to read the terms.

examples.said: Prima di aprire il conto, mi serve il Suo codice fiscale.
examples.en: Before we open the account, I need your tax ID number.

examples.said: Prima che tu parta, ti do il mio numero.
examples.en: Before you leave, I'll give you my number.

examples.said: Te la riporto prima che faccia buio.
examples.en: I'll bring it back before it gets dark.

steps.notice: When the same person does both things, it's prima di plus the -re form; when the other part is about someone else, or the weather, it's prima che plus the subjunctive, as in prima che tu parta.

ask.said: L'impiegato ti dà il contratto. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: The clerk hands you the contract. What do you tell him?

answer.said: Prima di firmare, vorrei leggere bene il contratto.
answer.en: Before I sign, I'd like to read the contract carefully.

ask.said: Parti domani. Cosa fai stasera?
ask.en: You're leaving tomorrow. What are you doing tonight?

answer.said: Prima di partire, faccio la valigia.
answer.en: I'm packing before I leave.

ask.said: La tua amica ti ha prestato la bici. Quando gliela riporti?
ask.en: Your friend lent you her bike. When will you bring it back to her?

answer.said: Gliela riporto prima che faccia buio.
answer.en: I'll bring it back to her before it gets dark.

mission.goal: Tell a friend you'll give them your number before they leave.

say.said: Prima che tu parta, ti do il mio numero.
say.en: Before you leave, I'll give you my number.

steps.title: Better?
steps.how_to: How to compare two options and say which one is the best.
steps.intro: You'll be able to weigh two apartments, or the train against the bus, and then say which one is the best. Italian uses più for "more" and il più for "the most."

examples.said: Questo è più luminoso dell'altro.
examples.en: This one's brighter than the other one.

examples.said: Il treno è più veloce del pullman.
examples.en: The train is faster than the bus.

examples.said: È l'albergo più tranquillo della zona.
examples.en: It's the quietest hotel in the area.

examples.said: Allora secondo me è il migliore.
examples.en: Then I think it's the best one.

steps.notice: Più plus di compares two things, as in più veloce del pullman; with il or la in front it picks the top one of a group, as in l'albergo più tranquillo della zona, and il migliore already means "the best."

ask.said: Per un weekend a Napoli, prendi il treno o il pullman? Perché?
ask.en: For a weekend in Naples, are you taking the train or the bus? Why?

answer.said: Prendo il treno, perché è più comodo del pullman.
answer.en: I'm taking the train, because it's more comfortable than the bus.

ask.said: Hai visto tre bilocali. Quale prendi?
ask.en: You saw three one-bedrooms. Which one are you taking?

answer.said: Prendo questo: è il più luminoso dei tre.
answer.en: I'm taking this one. It's the brightest of the three.

ask.said: Qui in zona, che bar consigli a un amico?
ask.en: Around here, which café would you recommend to a friend?

answer.said: Il bar … è il migliore della zona.
answer.en: … is the best café around here.

mission.goal: Tell a friend which apartment is the best.

say.said: Secondo me questo è il migliore.
say.en: I think this one's the best.

steps.title: How long
steps.how_to: How to say how long something has been going on, with da or sono … che.
steps.intro: To say how long something has been going on, Italian uses the present tense, with da or with sono … che. You'll use it to say how long you've lived here, or to chase a repair.

examples.said: Vivo in Italia da due anni.
examples.en: I've been living in Italy for two years.

examples.said: Da quanto tempo studia l'italiano?
examples.en: How long have you been studying Italian?

examples.said: Sono già due settimane che aspetto l'idraulico.
examples.en: I've been waiting for the plumber for two weeks already.

examples.said: È un mese che il citofono non funziona.
examples.en: The buzzer hasn't worked in a month.

steps.notice: For something that started in the past and is still going on, Italian uses the present, because it isn't over: vivo qui da due anni, or sono due anni che vivo qui; with one week or month, it's è.

ask.said: Da quanto tempo vivi in questa città?
ask.en: How long have you lived in this city?

answer.said: Vivo qui da …
answer.en: I've been living here for …

ask.said: È tanto che studi l'italiano?
ask.en: Have you been studying Italian long?

answer.said: Sono … mesi che studio l'italiano.
answer.en: I've been studying Italian for … months.

ask.said: La caldaia è ancora rotta. Cosa dici alla padrona di casa?
ask.en: The boiler's still broken. What do you tell your landlady?

answer.said: Sono dieci giorni che aspetto l'idraulico!
answer.en: I've been waiting ten days for the plumber!

mission.goal: Tell your landlady how long you've been waiting for the plumber.

say.said: Sono già due settimane che aspetto l'idraulico.
say.en: I've been waiting for the plumber for two weeks already.

steps.title: OK?
steps.how_to: How to ask what you're allowed to do with si può and si possono.
steps.intro: To ask if something's allowed, say si può and a verb; when a plural word follows, it becomes si possono: si possono fare foto?

examples.said: Scusi, si può entrare?
examples.en: Excuse me, is it okay to go in?

examples.said: Si possono fare foto?
examples.en: Can you take photos?

examples.said: Sì, ma non si può usare il flash.
examples.en: Yes, but you can't use the flash.

examples.said: Però durante la messa non si può girare per la chiesa.
examples.en: But you can't walk around the church during mass.

steps.notice: Si può with a verb asks or says what anyone may do there; with a plural like foto it becomes si possono, because the verb matches the plural.
steps.context: Churches are working places of worship, and during mass people come in to attend it.

ask.said: Sei alla porta di una chiesa. Cosa chiedi?
ask.en: You're at the door of a church. What do you ask?

answer.said: Scusi, si può visitare la chiesa adesso?
answer.en: Excuse me, is it okay to visit the church now?

ask.said: Vuoi fotografare gli affreschi. Cosa chiedi al custode?
ask.en: You want to photograph the frescoes. What do you ask the attendant?

answer.said: Si possono fotografare gli affreschi?
answer.en: Can you take pictures of the frescoes?

ask.said: La tua macchina fotografica ha il flash. Cosa chiedi?
ask.en: Your camera has a flash. What do you ask?

answer.said: Si può usare il flash?
answer.en: Can you use the flash?

mission.goal: Ask whether you can take photos inside a church.

say.said: Si possono fare foto?
say.en: Can you take photos?

steps.title: Give it to me
steps.how_to: How to say "it to me" and "it to you" with me lo, te la and the rest.
steps.intro: Two small words together, like me lo or te la, say "it to me" or "it to you." You'll use them to offer, lend and ask for things without naming them again.

examples.said: Me lo incarta, per favore? È un regalo.
examples.en: Could you wrap it for me, please? It's a gift.

examples.said: La torta? Te la porto stasera.
examples.en: The cake? I'll bring it over tonight.

examples.said: Se ti serve il trapano, te lo presto volentieri.
examples.en: If you need the drill, I'm happy to lend it to you.

examples.said: Le chiavi? Te le restituisco stasera.
examples.en: The keys? I'll give them back to you tonight.

steps.notice: The "to whom" word comes first and mi or ti become me or te, then lo, la, li or le for the thing, because it matches the thing: lo for the drill, le for the keys.
steps.context: In almost any shop you can say "È un regalo" and they'll gift-wrap it for free.

ask.said: Un amico ti chiede i tuoi libri. Cosa rispondi?
ask.en: A friend asks to borrow your books. What do you say?

answer.said: Te li presto volentieri.
answer.en: I'm happy to lend them to you.

ask.said: La tua vicina vuole indietro la sua scala. Cosa le dici?
ask.en: Your neighbor wants her ladder back. What do you tell her?

answer.said: Scusa, te la riporto subito.
answer.en: Sorry, I'll bring it right back.

ask.said: Compri una borsa per un'amica. Cosa chiedi alla commessa?
ask.en: You're buying a bag for a friend. What do you ask the salesclerk?

answer.said: Me la incarta, per favore?
answer.en: Could you wrap it for me, please?

mission.goal: Ask the shopkeeper to gift-wrap what you bought.

say.said: Me lo incarta, per favore? È un regalo.
say.en: Could you wrap it for me, please? It's a gift.

steps.title: Do it for someone
steps.how_to: How to offer to do something for someone with glielo and with posso.
steps.intro: Glielo means "it to him," "it to her," or "it to you" when you're being polite, and with posso these pairs make an offer: posso portartelo. You'll use them to offer to do things for people.

examples.said: Gliela incarto subito.
examples.en: I'll wrap it for you right away.

examples.said: Posso ordinarglielo. Arriva in due giorni.
examples.en: I can order it for you. It'll be here in two days.

examples.said: Posso portartelo stasera, se vuoi.
examples.en: I can bring it over tonight if you want.

examples.said: Glielo dico io.
examples.en: I'll tell him myself.

steps.notice: Gli, le and Le all become glie- and join the thing as one word, so glielo can mean to him, to her or to you. With posso, the pair goes before it or joins the end of the infinitive: te lo posso portare, posso portartelo.

ask.said: Il libraio ti chiede il numero di telefono. Cosa rispondi?
ask.en: The bookseller asks for your phone number. What do you say?

answer.said: Sì, glielo scrivo qui.
answer.en: Sure, I'll write it down for you here.

ask.said: Un'amica ha bisogno del tuo caricabatterie stasera. Cosa le dici?
ask.en: A friend needs your charger tonight. What do you tell her?

answer.said: Te lo posso portare stasera, se vuoi.
answer.en: I can bring it to you tonight if you want.

ask.said: La tua vicina anziana non riesce a leggere una lettera. Cosa le dici?
ask.en: Your elderly neighbor can't read a letter. What do you tell her?

answer.said: Posso leggergliela io, se vuole.
answer.en: I can read it to you, if you'd like.

mission.goal: Offer to bring something over to a friend.

say.said: Posso portartelo stasera, se vuoi.
say.en: I can bring it over tonight if you want.

steps.title: More?
steps.how_to: How to ask for some more of something with me ne.
steps.intro: Me ne dà means "could you give me some" or "could you give me two." It's what you say at the deli counter when you want more.

examples.said: È buonissimo. Me ne dà ancora un etto?
examples.en: It's delicious. Could I have another hundred grams?

examples.said: Me ne dà un pezzetto da assaggiare?
examples.en: Could I have a little piece to taste?

examples.said: Le piace? Ne vuole ancora?
examples.en: Do you like it? Would you like some more?

examples.said: Te ne porto due.
examples.en: I'll bring you two.

steps.notice: Ne means "of it" or "of them" and joins like lo, so mi becomes me: me ne dà un etto. With an amount, ne is always there, because the amount is of something.

ask.said: Il prosciutto è buonissimo. Cosa chiedi al salumiere?
ask.en: The prosciutto is delicious. What do you ask the deli man?

answer.said: Me ne dà ancora due fette?
answer.en: Could I have two more slices?

ask.said: Vuoi assaggiare il pecorino. Cosa chiedi?
ask.en: You want to taste the pecorino. What do you ask?

answer.said: Me ne dà un po' da assaggiare?
answer.en: Could I have a little to taste?

ask.said: Un amico non ha bicchieri per la festa. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: A friend doesn't have glasses for the party. What do you tell him?

answer.said: Te ne porto sei, se vuoi.
answer.en: I'll bring you six, if you want.

mission.goal: Ask for another hundred grams at the deli counter.

say.said: Me ne dà ancora un etto?
say.en: Could I have another hundred grams?

steps.title: I forgot
steps.how_to: How to say "I forgot about it" with me ne.
steps.intro: Verbs like dimenticarsi and ricordarsi take ne for "about it," as in me ne sono dimenticato. You'll use it to apologize and to check on things.

examples.said: Scusa, me ne sono dimenticato!
examples.en: Sorry, I forgot all about it!

examples.said: Il pane? Me ne sono dimenticata anch'io.
examples.en: The bread? I forgot about it too.

examples.said: La riunione di stasera? Te ne ricordi?
examples.en: The meeting tonight, you remember?

examples.said: La bolletta? Me ne dimentico sempre.
examples.en: The bill? I always forget about it.

steps.notice: Ne stands for "about it," so me ne, te ne and se ne come before the verb even where English has nothing. In the past, a woman says dimenticata.

ask.said: Marco doveva comprare il pane. L'ha comprato?
ask.en: Marco was supposed to buy bread. Did he?

answer.said: No, se n'è dimenticato.
answer.en: No, he forgot all about it.

ask.said: Non hai ancora riportato la scala alla vicina. Cosa le dici?
ask.en: You still haven't brought the ladder back to your neighbor. What do you tell her?

answer.said: Scusa, me ne dimentico ogni volta!
answer.en: Sorry, I forget every time!

ask.said: Un'amica doveva portare le chiavi. Cosa le chiedi?
ask.en: A friend was supposed to bring the keys. What do you ask her?

answer.said: Te ne sei ricordata?
answer.en: Did you remember?

mission.goal: Apologize to your neighbor for forgetting something.

say.said: Scusa, me ne sono dimenticato!
say.en: Sorry, I forgot all about it!

steps.title: Polite commands
steps.how_to: How to tell someone you call Lei what to do, or not to do.
steps.intro: This is how you tell someone you call Lei what to do or not to do, like a taxi driver or a stranger in the street. It uses the same forms as the present subjunctive.

examples.said: Giri alla prima a destra, per favore.
examples.en: Take the first right, please.

examples.said: Prenda il primo autobus che passa.
examples.en: Take the first bus that comes.

examples.said: Non prenda il 40, oggi non passa.
examples.en: Don't take the 40, it's not running today.

examples.said: Non si preoccupi, Le tengo io il posto.
examples.en: Don't worry, I'll save your seat.

steps.notice: With Lei, verbs ending in -are take an -i (giri) and the others take an -a (prenda), and andare becomes vada, because this command is really the subjunctive. To say don't, just put non in front: non prenda.
steps.context: In most Italian cities you take a taxi from a rank or book one by phone or app.

ask.said: Sei in taxi e il tassista non conosce la tua via. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: You're in a taxi and the driver doesn't know your street. What do you tell him?

answer.said: Giri alla seconda a sinistra, per favore.
answer.en: Take the second left, please.

ask.said: Un turista anziano ti chiede la strada per la piazza. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: An older tourist asks you the way to the piazza. What do you tell him?

answer.said: Vada sempre dritto, poi giri a destra.
answer.en: Go straight ahead, then turn right.

ask.said: Il tuo vicino aspetta un pacco, ma domani non è a casa. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: Your neighbor is expecting a package, but he won't be home tomorrow. What do you tell him?

answer.said: Non si preoccupi, glielo prendo io.
answer.en: Don't worry, I'll take it in for you.

mission.goal: Give a taxi driver directions to your street.

say.said: Giri alla prima a destra, per favore.
say.en: Take the first right, please.

steps.title: Invite politely
steps.how_to: How to invite someone you call Lei to come in, sit down or go ahead.
steps.intro: Today you'll invite someone you call Lei to come in or sit down, the way staff and hosts invite you. You'll hear mi dica and si accomodi at every office and front door.

examples.said: Buongiorno, mi dica.
examples.en: Good morning, how can I help you?

examples.said: Prego, si sieda.
examples.en: Please, sit down.

examples.said: Entri pure!
examples.en: Come on in!

examples.said: Mi dia pure la borsa, gliela tengo io.
examples.en: Go ahead and give me your bag, I'll hold it for you.

steps.notice: With Lei, mi and si go before the verb: mi dica, si sieda, si accomodi. Prego before the verb or pure after it turns the command into an invitation; here pure means "go ahead," not "also."

ask.said: Un vicino anziano bussa alla tua porta e dice: "Permesso?" Cosa rispondi?
ask.en: An older neighbor knocks on your door and says, "May I come in?" What do you say?

answer.said: Prego, entri pure!
answer.en: Please, come on in!

ask.said: Una signora anziana entra e cerca una sedia. Cosa le dici?
ask.en: An older woman comes in, looking for a chair. What do you say to her?

answer.said: Prego, si accomodi.
answer.en: Please, have a seat.

ask.said: Una signora cerca i soldi e ti chiede scusa. Cosa le dici?
ask.en: A woman is looking for her money and apologizes to you. What do you tell her?

answer.said: Faccia pure con calma.
answer.en: Take your time.

mission.goal: Invite an older neighbor into your home.

say.said: Prego, entri pure!
say.en: Please, come on in!

steps.title: Everyone
steps.how_to: How to say a few, everyone and something with qualche, ognuno and qualcosa di.
steps.intro: These words help you talk about how many or which ones without counting: a few minutes, everyone, something hot. You'll hear them at counters and in waiting rooms.

examples.said: Aspetti qualche minuto, per favore, c'è un po' di fila.
examples.en: Please wait a few minutes, there's a bit of a line.

examples.said: C'è qualche problema?
examples.en: Is there a problem?

examples.said: Ognuno ha il suo numero: adesso tocca al quarantadue.
examples.en: Everyone has a number, and now they're on forty-two.

examples.said: Desidera qualcosa di caldo?
examples.en: Would you like something hot?

steps.notice: Qualche means "a few" or "some" but always takes a singular noun: qualche minuto. Ognuno means "everyone," and qualcosa di plus a describing word means "something" of that kind.

ask.said: Dal medico, di solito quanto aspetti?
ask.en: How long do you usually wait at the doctor's?

answer.said: Di solito aspetto qualche minuto.
answer.en: I usually wait a few minutes.

ask.said: Fa freddo e sei al bar. Cosa vuoi bere?
ask.en: It's cold and you're at the café. What do you want to drink?

answer.said: Vorrei qualcosa di caldo.
answer.en: I'd like something hot.

ask.said: In sala d'attesa, come sai quando tocca a te?
ask.en: In the waiting room, how do you know when it's your turn?

answer.said: Ognuno ha il suo numero.
answer.en: Everyone has their own number.

mission.goal: Order something hot to drink.

say.said: Vorrei qualcosa di caldo, per favore.
say.en: I'd like something hot, please.

steps.title: My work
steps.how_to: How to say what your job is and what field you work in.
steps.intro: Today you'll answer one of the first questions people ask here: what do you do? There are a few ways to say it.

examples.said: Io sono ingegnere. E Lei, di cosa si occupa?
examples.en: I'm an engineer. And what do you do?

examples.said: Lavoro come insegnante.
examples.en: I work as a teacher.

examples.said: Io mi occupo di marketing.
examples.en: I work in marketing.

steps.notice: Say your job with sono and no word for "a": sono ingegnere. You can also say lavoro come, or mi occupo di for a field.

ask.said: Che lavoro fai?
ask.en: What do you do for a living?

answer.said: Lavoro come …
answer.en: I work as a …

ask.said: In che campo lavori?
ask.en: What field are you in?

answer.said: Mi occupo di …
answer.en: I work in …

ask.said: Che lavoro vorresti fare in Italia?
ask.en: What job would you like to do in Italy?

answer.said: Vorrei lavorare come …
answer.en: I'd like to work as a …

mission.goal: Tell a neighbor what you do for a living.

say.said: Mi occupo di marketing.
say.en: I work in marketing.

steps.title: Then suddenly
steps.how_to: How to set the scene of a story and then say what happened.
steps.intro: You'll be able to tell a story the way people do here: first how things were or what you were doing, then what happened. The scene goes in the imperfetto, or stavo with an -ando form, and the event in the passato prossimo.

examples.said: Stavo cucinando quando è saltata la luce.
examples.en: I was cooking when the power went out.

examples.said: Io stavo per andare a letto quando è saltata la luce.
examples.en: I was about to go to bed when the power went out.

examples.said: Quando siamo arrivati, la camera era sporca e faceva freddo.
examples.en: When we got there, the room was dirty and it was cold.

examples.said: Il treno stava per partire quando ho trovato il binario.
examples.en: The train was about to leave when I found the platform.

steps.notice: Era, faceva and stavo cucinando set the scene, and stavo per means it was just about to; è saltata and ho trovato tell what happened, because it's one event at one moment.

ask.said: Ieri sera è saltata la luce. Tu cosa facevi?
ask.en: The power went out last night. What were you doing?

answer.said: Stavo guardando un film quando è saltata la luce.
answer.en: I was watching a movie when the power went out.

ask.said: Ti ho chiamato alle undici. Dormivi già?
ask.en: I called you at eleven. Were you already asleep?

answer.said: No, ma stavo per andare a dormire.
answer.en: No, but I was about to go to sleep.

ask.said: Pensa a un viaggio andato male. Cosa è successo?
ask.en: Think of a trip that went badly. What happened?

answer.said: La camera era sporca e ho chiamato la reception.
answer.en: The room was dirty, and I called the front desk.

mission.goal: Tell a neighbor what you were doing when the power went out.

say.said: Stavo cucinando quando è saltata la luce.
say.en: I was cooking when the power went out.

steps.title: Already
steps.how_to: How to say one thing had already happened before another.
steps.intro: When you tell a story, you'll be able to say what had already happened by then, like the train had already left. It's the trapassato: the imperfetto of avere or essere plus the past participle.

examples.said: Quando siamo arrivati, il treno era già partito.
examples.en: When we got there, the train had already left.

examples.said: Sul treno ho capito che avevo dimenticato il caricabatterie a casa.
examples.en: On the train I realized I'd left my charger at home.

examples.said: Non avevo mai visto tanta gente.
examples.en: I'd never seen so many people.

examples.said: Quando è saltata la luce, avevo già cenato.
examples.en: When the power went out, I'd already had dinner.

steps.notice: Era partito and avevo dimenticato put one past event before another, because it happened first; essere and avere work just as in the passato prossimo.

ask.said: Ieri hai perso il treno. Perché?
ask.en: You missed your train yesterday. Why?

answer.said: Quando ho trovato il binario, il treno era già partito.
answer.en: By the time I found the platform, the train had already left.

ask.said: Sul treno hai aperto lo zaino. Cosa mancava?
ask.en: On the train you opened your backpack. What was missing?

answer.said: Avevo dimenticato il caricabatterie a casa.
answer.en: I'd left my charger at home.

ask.said: Cosa hai visto qui in Italia per la prima volta?
ask.en: What did you see here in Italy for the first time?

answer.said: Non avevo mai visto tanta gente in piazza.
answer.en: I'd never seen so many people in a piazza.

mission.goal: Tell a friend about a time you got there too late.

say.said: Quando siamo arrivati, il treno era già partito.
say.en: When we got there, the train had already left.

steps.title: Because
steps.how_to: How to give the reason for something and what came of it.
steps.intro: You'll be able to link why something happened and what happened next when you tell a story. Siccome and visto che open with the reason, perché gives it after, and quindi, perciò and così bring in the result.

examples.said: Siccome pioveva, abbiamo preso un taxi.
examples.en: Since it was raining, we took a taxi.

examples.said: Abbiamo preso un taxi perché pioveva.
examples.en: We took a taxi because it was raining.

examples.said: Visto che c'era sciopero, siamo andati a piedi.
examples.en: Since there was a strike, we walked.

examples.said: Ormai era tardi, quindi ho cenato con pane e formaggio.
examples.en: By then it was late, so I had bread and cheese for dinner.

steps.notice: Siccome and visto che put the reason first, perché puts it after what happened, and quindi brings in the result, so you can tell the same story in either order.
steps.context: Strikes are announced days in advance, and a story that starts with c'era sciopero is one every Italian recognizes.

ask.said: Ieri pioveva tanto. Come hai fatto a tornare a casa?
ask.en: It poured yesterday. How did you get home?

answer.said: Siccome pioveva, ho preso un taxi.
answer.en: Since it was raining, I took a taxi.

ask.said: Perché non hai preso l'autobus?
ask.en: Why didn't you take the bus?

answer.said: Non ho preso l'autobus perché c'era sciopero.
answer.en: I didn't take the bus because there was a strike.

ask.said: Ieri c'era lo sciopero dei treni. Cosa hai fatto?
ask.en: There was a train strike yesterday. What did you do?

answer.said: C'era sciopero, quindi ho preso il pullman.
answer.en: There was a strike, so I took the bus.

mission.goal: Tell a friend why something went wrong and what you did.

say.said: Siccome c'era sciopero, ho preso un taxi.
say.en: Since there was a strike, I took a taxi.

steps.title: Nobody
steps.how_to: How to say nobody did something, with nessuno first or after the verb.
steps.intro: When something goes wrong on a trip, you'll want to say nobody came or nobody helped. Nessuno can start the sentence or come after the verb.

examples.said: Nessuno ci ha aiutato.
examples.en: Nobody helped us.

examples.said: Davvero? Non vi ha aiutato nessuno?
examples.en: Really? Nobody helped you?

examples.said: Non c'era nessuno alla reception.
examples.en: There was nobody at the front desk.

examples.said: E poi non è venuto nessuno?
examples.en: And then nobody came?

steps.notice: Both ways mean the same thing: at the start, nessuno stands on its own; after the verb, it goes with non before the verb, so the sentence is negative from the beginning.

ask.said: Quando hai fatto il check-in, chi c'era alla reception?
ask.en: When you checked in, who was at the front desk?

answer.said: Alla reception non c'era nessuno.
answer.en: There was nobody at the front desk.

ask.said: Hai chiamato la reception due volte. Chi ti ha aiutato?
ask.en: You called the front desk twice. Who helped you?

answer.said: Nessuno mi ha aiutato.
answer.en: Nobody helped me.

ask.said: E dopo la seconda telefonata, è venuto qualcuno?
ask.en: And after the second call, did anyone come?

answer.said: No, non è venuto nessuno.
answer.en: No, nobody came.

mission.goal: Tell a friend about a stay where nobody helped you.

say.said: Nessuno ci ha aiutato.
say.en: Nobody helped us.

steps.title: I'll manage
steps.how_to: How to talk about coping: making it, getting by, heading off, not letting things get to you.
steps.intro: Some everyday verbs come with two little words attached, like ce la faccio or me la cavo, and they're how people here talk about coping. You'll be able to say you can make it, you're getting by, you're heading off, and tell someone not to let it get to them.

examples.said: Ce la fai per le otto?
examples.en: Can you make it by eight?

examples.said: Me la cavo, grazie.
examples.en: I'm managing, thanks.

examples.said: Domani mattina ce ne andiamo presto.
examples.en: We're leaving early tomorrow morning.

examples.said: Non te la prendere, capita.
examples.en: Don't let it get to you, it happens.

steps.notice: The little words are part of each verb and don't mean 'it' or 'there' anymore, and the first one changes with the person: ce la faccio, ce la fai; me la cavo, te la cavi.

ask.said: Domani il treno parte alle sette. Riesci a essere in stazione in tempo?
ask.en: The train leaves at seven tomorrow. Can you get to the station in time?

answer.said: Sì, ce la faccio.
answer.en: Yes, I can make it.

ask.said: Come va con l'italiano qui?
ask.en: How's your Italian going here?

answer.said: Me la cavo, ma parlo ancora piano.
answer.en: I'm getting by, but I still talk slowly.

ask.said: Un amico ha perso il treno ed è arrabbiato. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: A friend missed his train and he's upset. What do you tell him?

answer.said: Dai, non te la prendere. Prendi il prossimo.
answer.en: Come on, don't let it get to you. Catch the next one.

mission.goal: Tell someone how you're getting on with Italian.

say.said: Me la cavo, grazie.
say.en: I'm getting by, thanks.

steps.title: I mean…
steps.how_to: How to say something another way, and ask what someone means.
steps.intro: When someone misunderstands you, or you don't follow them, you'll be able to clear it up in Italian instead of switching to English.

examples.said: In che senso? Mi spieghi?
examples.en: What do you mean? Can you explain?

examples.said: Cioè, voglio dire che è stancante.
examples.en: I mean, what I'm saying is it's tiring.

examples.said: Ah, nel senso che non hai tempo?
examples.en: Oh, meaning you don't have time?

examples.said: Mi spiego meglio: sono quattro ore di fila, senza pausa.
examples.en: Let me put it another way: it's four hours straight, with no break.

steps.notice: Cioè, voglio dire, nel senso che and mi spiego meglio let you say the same thing another way, and in che senso? asks the other person to do it.

ask.said: Hai detto che il corso è pesante. È difficile?
ask.en: You said the course is a grind. Is it hard?

answer.said: No, cioè, non è difficile. Voglio dire che è lungo.
answer.en: No, I mean, it's not hard. What I'm saying is it's long.

ask.said: Non capisci cosa vuole dire un amico. Cosa gli chiedi?
ask.en: You don't get what a friend means. What do you ask him?

answer.said: In che senso? Cosa vuoi dire?
answer.en: What do you mean? What are you trying to say?

ask.said: Il tuo amico non ha ancora capito. Cosa dici?
ask.en: Your friend still doesn't get it. What do you say?

answer.said: Mi spiego meglio: sono tante ore, senza pausa.
answer.en: Let me put it another way: it's a lot of hours, with no break.

mission.goal: When someone doesn't follow you, say it another way in Italian.

say.said: Mi spiego meglio.
say.en: Let me put it another way.

steps.title: Local history
steps.how_to: How to follow a local telling the history of a place.
steps.intro: When a local tells you a place's history, you'll hear a past tense kept for long-ago events, like nacque and morì, and centuries named by their hundreds, like il Trecento for the 1300s. You mainly need to recognize the verbs; when you speak, your usual past tense is fine.

examples.said: Mio nonno raccontava che la piazza nacque nel Medioevo, come mercato.
examples.en: My grandfather used to say the square started out as a market in the Middle Ages.

examples.said: Dicono che nel Cinquecento una famiglia di banchieri rifece tutta la piazza.
examples.en: They say a family of bankers rebuilt the whole square in the 1500s.

examples.said: Il Cinquecento è il sedicesimo secolo, vero?
examples.en: The Cinquecento is the sixteenth century, right?

examples.said: Il mercante morì senza figli e lasciò tutto alla città.
examples.en: The merchant died without children and left everything to the town.

steps.notice: Nacque, morì and lasciò are the past tense of stories about long ago, and mean the same as è nato, è morto and ha lasciato. A century goes by its hundreds, so il Cinquecento is the 1500s, the sixteenth century.

ask.said: Questo affresco è del 1350. Di che secolo è?
ask.en: This fresco is from 1350. What century is that?

answer.said: È del Trecento.
answer.en: It's from the 1300s.

ask.said: Senti questa parola: costruì. È passato o futuro?
ask.en: Listen to this word: costruì. Is it past or future?

answer.said: È passato: vuol dire 'ha costruito'.
answer.en: It's past. It means the same as 'ha costruito', he built.

ask.said: Senti: 'Michelangelo nacque nel 1475.' Cosa vuol dire?
ask.en: Listen: 'Michelangelo nacque nel 1475.' What does that mean?

answer.said: Vuol dire che Michelangelo è nato nel 1475, nel Quattrocento.
answer.en: It means Michelangelo was born in 1475, in the 1400s.

mission.goal: Get a local to tell you a story about the town, and keep it going.

say.said: E cos'è successo?
say.en: And what happened?

steps.title: Who made it?
steps.how_to: How to ask when something was built or who painted it.
steps.intro: To say something 'was built' or 'was painted', Italian uses essere with a word like costruita or dipinto that matches the building or the picture. The person who did it comes after da.

examples.said: Scusi, quando è stata costruita questa chiesa?
examples.en: Excuse me, when was this church built?

examples.said: E questo affresco, da chi è stato dipinto?
examples.en: And who painted this fresco?

examples.said: È stato dipinto da un allievo di Giotto.
examples.en: It was painted by one of Giotto's pupils.

examples.said: Sa che questo palazzo è stato costruito da una famiglia di banchieri?
examples.en: Did you know this building was built by a family of bankers?

steps.notice: Each line uses è stata or è stato with costruita or dipinto, matching la chiesa or l'affresco, and the painter comes after da, because the line is about the thing, not the person.
steps.context: In many churches the lights for the frescoes in side chapels run on coins.

ask.said: Vedi una chiesa antica. Cosa chiedi?
ask.en: You see an old church. What do you ask?

answer.said: Scusi, sa quando è stata costruita questa chiesa?
answer.en: Excuse me, do you know when this church was built?

ask.said: Ti piace un affresco, ma non conosci il pittore. Cosa chiedi?
ask.en: You like a fresco, but you don't know the painter. What do you ask?

answer.said: Da chi è stato dipinto questo affresco?
answer.en: Who painted this fresco?

ask.said: Un amico ti chiede chi ha fatto questo quadro. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: A friend asks you who did this painting. What do you tell him?

answer.said: È stato dipinto da Caravaggio.
answer.en: It was painted by Caravaggio.

mission.goal: Ask a local when the church on the square was built.

say.said: Scusi, quando è stata costruita questa chiesa?
say.en: Excuse me, when was this church built?

steps.title: I think
steps.how_to: How to say what you think or hope when you're not sure.
steps.intro: You'll be able to say what you think or hope when you're not sure: I think it's closed, I hope he comes. After penso che, credo che and spero che the verb is in the subjunctive: -are verbs take -i, the others -a, and a few have their own forms, like sia, abbia and venga.

examples.said: Domani è lunedì. Penso che il museo sia chiuso.
examples.en: Tomorrow's Monday. I think the museum's closed.

examples.said: Spero che venga anche Marco.
examples.en: I hope Marco comes too.

examples.said: Credo che abbiano ragione.
examples.en: I think they're right.

examples.said: Penso che tu abbia ragione.
examples.en: I think you're right.

steps.notice: After penso che, credo che and spero che the verb changes: sia, venga, abbia, because it's what you think or hope, not a fact. Io, tu and lei share one form, so add tu when you mean the person you're talking to.
steps.context: Many museums and shops close one day a week, often Monday, so penso che sia chiuso is a guess you'll make a lot.

ask.said: Oggi è lunedì. Il museo è aperto?
ask.en: It's Monday today. Is the museum open?

answer.said: Credo che oggi sia chiuso.
answer.en: I think it's closed today.

ask.said: Che tempo farà domenica?
ask.en: What's the weather going to be like on Sunday?

answer.said: Spero che faccia bel tempo.
answer.en: I hope it'll be nice out.

ask.said: Il tuo vicino parla inglese?
ask.en: Does your neighbor speak English?

answer.said: Credo che parli un po' d'inglese.
answer.en: I think he speaks a little English.

mission.goal: Guess with someone whether a place is open today.

say.said: Penso che sia chiuso il lunedì.
say.en: I think it's closed on Mondays.

steps.title: It's true
steps.how_to: How to state a fact or give your view straight out.
steps.intro: You'll be able to say what you know for sure, or give your view plainly. So che, sono sicuro che, è vero che and secondo me take the ordinary verb forms, the indicative.

examples.said: So che è chiuso il lunedì.
examples.en: I know it's closed on Mondays.

examples.said: Secondo me è chiuso.
examples.en: If you ask me, it's closed.

examples.said: È vero che qui si cena tardi.
examples.en: It's true people eat late here.

examples.said: Secondo me è un po' caro.
examples.en: If you ask me, it's a little expensive.

steps.notice: So che, è vero che and secondo me present something as a fact or a plain view, so the verb stays as usual: è chiuso, si cena.

ask.said: Secondo te, quel ristorante è caro?
ask.en: Do you think that restaurant is expensive?

answer.said: Secondo me è un po' caro, ma si mangia bene.
answer.en: If you ask me, it's a little pricey, but the food is good.

ask.said: Hai controllato gli orari del museo. È aperto il martedì?
ask.en: You checked the museum's hours. Is it open on Tuesdays?

answer.said: No, so che è chiuso il martedì.
answer.en: No, I know it's closed on Tuesdays.

ask.said: A che ora si cena al sud?
ask.en: What time do people eat dinner in the south?

answer.said: So che al sud si cena verso le nove o le dieci.
answer.en: I know in the south people eat around nine or ten.

mission.goal: Give a friend your opinion of a restaurant.

say.said: Secondo me è un po' caro.
say.en: If you ask me, it's a little expensive.

steps.title: Give advice
steps.how_to: How to give a friend advice.
steps.intro: You'll be able to give a friend advice two ways: it's best if you..., or if I were you, I'd.... After è meglio che and è importante che the verb is in the subjunctive; after se fossi in te comes the 'would' form.

examples.said: Dai, è importante che tu ti muova un po' ogni giorno.
examples.en: Come on, it's important for you to move around a bit every day.

examples.said: Se fossi in te, studierei di più.
examples.en: If I were you, I'd study more.

examples.said: È meglio che tu non beva caffè la sera.
examples.en: It's better if you don't drink coffee in the evening.

examples.said: Se fossi in te, chiederei alla padrona di casa.
examples.en: If I were you, I'd ask the landlady.

steps.notice: Advice to a friend takes che plus the subjunctive (beva, muova), or se fossi in te plus the 'would' form (studierei, chiederei). Se fossi in te never changes, because you're putting yourself in their place.

ask.said: Un amico dorme male. Cosa gli consigli?
ask.en: A friend is sleeping badly. What would you tell him?

answer.said: Se fossi in te, non berrei caffè la sera.
answer.en: If I were you, I wouldn't drink coffee in the evening.

ask.said: Un'amica non fa mai sport. Cosa le dici?
ask.en: A friend never exercises. What do you tell her?

answer.said: È importante che tu faccia un po' di movimento ogni giorno.
answer.en: It's important for you to get some exercise every day.

ask.said: Un'amica deve pagare un affitto più alto. Cosa le consigli?
ask.en: A friend's rent is going up. What do you suggest?

answer.said: Se fossi in te, cercherei un'altra casa.
answer.en: If I were you, I'd look for another place.

mission.goal: Give a friend advice about sleeping better.

say.said: È meglio che tu non beva caffè la sera.
say.en: It's better if you don't drink coffee in the evening.

steps.title: As long as
steps.how_to: How to agree to something as long as, or unless, something happens.
steps.intro: You'll be able to agree to something on a condition, like lending your bike as long as it comes back tonight. Purché means as long as, a meno che non means unless, and both take the subjunctive.

examples.said: Ti presto la bici, purché tu me la riporti stasera.
examples.en: I'll lend you the bike, as long as you bring it back tonight.

examples.said: A meno che non piova, domani andiamo al mare.
examples.en: Unless it rains, we'll go to the beach tomorrow.

examples.said: Promesso. A meno che non me la rubino al mercato!
examples.en: I promise. Unless someone steals it at the market!

steps.notice: Purché sets the condition and a meno che non names what would stop it; both take the subjunctive (riporti, piova), and the non after a meno che doesn't make it negative.

ask.said: Un'amica ti chiede la bici. Cosa le rispondi?
ask.en: A friend asks to borrow your bike. What do you tell her?

answer.said: Te la presto, purché tu me la riporti stasera.
answer.en: I'll lend it to you, as long as you bring it back tonight.

ask.said: Domani andiamo al mare?
ask.en: Should we go to the beach tomorrow?

answer.said: Sì, a meno che non piova.
answer.en: Yes, unless it rains.

ask.said: Un amico vuole la tua macchina per il weekend. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: A friend wants your car for the weekend. What do you tell him?

answer.said: Te la presto, purché tu me la riporti domenica.
answer.en: I'll lend it to you, as long as you bring it back on Sunday.

mission.goal: Lend a friend something on a condition.

say.said: Te la presto, purché tu me la riporti stasera.
say.en: I'll lend it to you, as long as you bring it back tonight.

steps.title: Hope it went well
steps.how_to: How to hope or think something has already happened.
steps.intro: You'll be able to say you hope someone slept well, or think someone has already arrived. It's the past subjunctive: abbia or sia plus the past participle.

examples.said: Spero che tu abbia dormito bene.
examples.en: I hope you slept well.

examples.said: Credo che sia già arrivata.
examples.en: I think she's already here.

examples.said: Non penso che abbiano capito.
examples.en: I don't think they understood.

examples.said: Penso che Anna sia arrivata ieri.
examples.en: I think Anna got here yesterday.

steps.notice: After spero che, credo che and penso che, something already done takes abbia or sia plus the participle, and with sia the participle agrees, just as in Anna è arrivata.

ask.said: Un'amica ieri sera era molto stanca. Cosa le dici stamattina?
ask.en: A friend was really tired last night. What do you say to her this morning?

answer.said: Ciao! Spero che tu abbia riposato bene.
answer.en: Hi! I hope you got some good rest.

ask.said: Anna doveva arrivare alle dieci. Dov'è, secondo te?
ask.en: Anna was supposed to arrive at ten. Where do you think she is?

answer.said: Penso che sia già arrivata a casa.
answer.en: I think she's already gotten home.

ask.said: Hai spiegato la strada a due turisti. Hanno capito?
ask.en: You gave two tourists directions. Did they understand?

answer.said: Non credo che abbiano capito bene.
answer.en: I don't think they really understood.

mission.goal: Greet a friend by saying you hope they slept well.

say.said: Spero che tu abbia dormito bene.
say.en: I hope you slept well.

steps.title: Say how you feel
steps.how_to: How to say how you feel about something: glad, sorry or afraid.
steps.intro: You'll be able to say how you feel about something: glad, sorry or afraid. When someone else does it, add che and the subjunctive; when you do it yourself, add di and the plain verb.

examples.said: Sono contenta che tu sia qui.
examples.en: I'm glad you're here.

examples.said: Mi dispiace molto che stia male.
examples.en: I'm so sorry he's not well.

examples.said: Sono contento di vederti!
examples.en: I'm so glad to see you!

examples.said: Mi dispiace di non poter venire.
examples.en: I'm sorry I can't come.

steps.notice: Use che and the subjunctive for what someone else does (che tu sia qui), and di and the plain verb for what you do yourself (di vederti).

ask.said: Una tua amica è malata. Cosa le dici?
ask.en: A friend of yours is sick. What do you say to her?

answer.said: Mi dispiace che tu stia male.
answer.en: I'm sorry you're not feeling well.

ask.said: Un amico ti invita a cena, ma hai già un impegno. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: A friend invites you to dinner, but you already have plans. What do you tell him?

answer.said: Mi dispiace di non poter venire, ho già un impegno.
answer.en: I'm sorry I can't come, I already have plans.

ask.said: Domani hai un esame. Come ti senti?
ask.en: You have an exam tomorrow. How do you feel?

answer.said: Ho paura di sbagliare.
answer.en: I'm afraid of getting it wrong.

mission.goal: Tell a neighbor you're sorry her husband is ill.

say.said: Mi dispiace molto che stia male.
say.en: I'm so sorry he's not well.

steps.title: How great!
steps.how_to: How to react to news in a word or two.
steps.intro: Today you'll react to news in a word or two, the way people do the moment they hear it: what a shame, what luck. They all start with che.

examples.said: Che bella notizia!
examples.en: What great news!

examples.said: Che peccato!
examples.en: What a shame!

examples.said: Che fortuna!
examples.en: How lucky!

steps.notice: Che plus a noun, or che plus a describing word and a noun, makes an exclamation. There's no word for "a": che bella notizia.

ask.said: Un'amica ha trovato lavoro a Milano. Cosa le dici?
ask.en: A friend has found a job in Milan. What do you say to her?

answer.said: Ma che bella notizia!
answer.en: Oh, what great news!

ask.said: Un amico non può venire alla tua festa. Cosa dici?
ask.en: A friend can't come to your party. What do you say?

answer.said: Oh, che peccato!
answer.en: Oh, what a shame!

ask.said: Un amico ha trovato una casa in centro a buon prezzo. Cosa dici?
ask.en: A friend found a place downtown at a good price. What do you say?

answer.said: Che fortuna! E a buon prezzo!
answer.en: How lucky! And at a good price!

mission.goal: React to a friend's good news.

say.said: Che bella notizia!
say.en: What great news!

steps.title: Good luck
steps.how_to: How to wish someone luck or offer sympathy, and how to answer.
steps.intro: Now you'll learn the set phrases for big moments, each with its own reply: good luck, best wishes and condolences.

examples.said: In bocca al lupo per il colloquio!
examples.en: Good luck with the interview!

examples.said: Crepi!
examples.en: Thanks!

examples.said: Tanti auguri!
examples.en: Best wishes!

examples.said: Le mie condoglianze.
examples.en: I'm so sorry for your loss.

steps.notice: These phrases come with set replies: you answer in bocca al lupo with crepi, and tanti auguri with grazie. Condoglianze is what you say when someone has died.
steps.context: Italians say auguri for birthdays, weddings, births and holidays, and in bocca al lupo before any exam or interview.

ask.said: Domani un tuo amico ha un esame. Cosa gli dici?
ask.en: A friend of yours has an exam tomorrow. What do you say to him?

answer.said: In bocca al lupo per l'esame!
answer.en: Good luck on your exam!

ask.said: Un'amica ti dice: "In bocca al lupo!" Cosa rispondi?
ask.en: A friend says to you, "Good luck!" What do you answer?

answer.said: Crepi, grazie!
answer.en: Thanks so much!

ask.said: Oggi è il compleanno della tua vicina. Cosa le dici?
ask.en: Today is your neighbor's birthday. What do you say to her?

answer.said: Tanti auguri di buon compleanno!
answer.en: Happy birthday!

mission.goal: Wish a friend good luck before an exam.

say.said: In bocca al lupo per l'esame!
say.en: Good luck on your exam!

steps.title: Imagine
steps.how_to: How to say what happens if, and show whether it's likely or only imagined.
steps.intro: You'll be able to talk about what happens if: if I have time, I'll come; if I won, I'd buy a house. For something likely, se takes the present; for something you're only imagining, se takes the -ssi form, then the 'would' form.

examples.said: Cosa faresti se vincessi alla lotteria?
examples.en: What would you do if you won the lottery?

examples.said: Se vincessi, comprerei una casa in campagna con un orto.
examples.en: If I won, I'd buy a house in the country with a vegetable garden.

examples.said: Se piove, resto a casa.
examples.en: If it rains, I'll stay home.

examples.said: Se piovesse, resterei a casa.
examples.en: If it rained, I'd stay home.

steps.notice: Se plus the present means you think it may well happen (se piove, resto); se plus the -ssi form and then the 'would' form means you're only imagining it (se piovesse, resterei). Hold the double s.
steps.context: Lots of city people dream of an orto, a small vegetable garden, and many rent a plot from the town.

ask.said: Ti invito a cena domani. Vieni?
ask.en: I'm inviting you to dinner tomorrow. Will you come?

answer.said: Se ho tempo, vengo volentieri.
answer.en: If I have time, I'd love to come.

ask.said: Come sarebbe la tua vita in campagna?
ask.en: What would your life be like in the country?

answer.said: Se abitassi in campagna, avrei un orto.
answer.en: If I lived in the country, I'd have a vegetable garden.

ask.said: Questa settimana lavori tutti i giorni. Vieni lo stesso alla festa?
ask.en: You're working every day this week. Are you still coming to the party?

answer.said: Purtroppo no. Se avessi tempo, verrei.
answer.en: Unfortunately not. If I had time, I'd come.

mission.goal: Answer an invitation by saying whether you'll have time.

say.said: Se ho tempo, vengo.
say.en: If I have time, I'll come.

steps.title: I'd like you to
steps.how_to: How to say what you'd like someone else to do with vorrei che.
steps.intro: When you'd like someone else to do something, say vorrei che and then the -ssi form: vorrei che tu venissi, I'd like you to come.

examples.said: Vorrei che tu venissi con me a Firenze sabato.
examples.en: I'd like you to come to Florence with me on Saturday.

examples.said: Peccato! Vorrei che venissi anche tu.
examples.en: Too bad! I wish you were coming too.

examples.said: Vorrei che fosse tutto più semplice!
examples.en: I wish it were all simpler!

steps.notice: After vorrei che the verb takes the -ssi form, like venissi or fosse, because it's a wish, not a fact.

ask.said: Sabato vai a Firenze. Cosa dici a un amico?
ask.en: You're going to Florence on Saturday. What do you tell a friend?

answer.said: Vorrei che tu venissi con me.
answer.en: I'd like you to come with me.

ask.said: Hai una settimana difficile. Cosa vorresti?
ask.en: You're having a hard week. What would you like?

answer.said: Vorrei che la settimana fosse più tranquilla.
answer.en: I wish this week were calmer.

ask.said: Un amico non può venire alla festa. Cosa gli rispondi?
ask.en: A friend can't come to the party. What do you say?

answer.said: Che peccato, vorrei che ci fossi anche tu.
answer.en: That's too bad, I wish you could be there too.

mission.goal: Ask a friend to come somewhere with you.

say.said: Vorrei che tu venissi con me.
say.en: I'd like you to come with me.

steps.title: If only
steps.how_to: How to say 'if only' and 'I wish' with magari.
steps.intro: Magari on its own is a quick 'if only!' Add the -ssi form and it becomes a wish: magari avessi più tempo!

examples.said: Magari vincessimo davvero!
examples.en: If only we actually won!

examples.said: Magari! Ma prima dovremmo comprare un biglietto.
examples.en: If only! But first we'd have to buy a ticket.

examples.said: Magari avessi più tempo!
examples.en: If only I had more time!

steps.notice: Magari alone answers a hope with 'if only!'; followed by the -ssi form, like avessi or vincessimo, it wishes for something you don't have, because it's a wish, not a fact.
steps.context: A big Superenalotto jackpot is national news, and what you'd do if you won is a classic chat at the bar.

ask.said: Pensi di vincere alla lotteria?
ask.en: Do you think you'll win the lottery?

answer.said: Magari! Ma prima dovrei comprare un biglietto.
answer.en: If only! But first I'd have to buy a ticket.

ask.said: Hai abbastanza tempo per studiare?
ask.en: Do you have enough time to study?

answer.said: No, magari avessi più tempo per studiare!
answer.en: No, I wish I had more time to study!

ask.said: Ti piacerebbe abitare in campagna?
ask.en: Would you like to live in the country?

answer.said: Magari abitassi in campagna!
answer.en: If only I lived in the country!

mission.goal: Wish out loud for something you don't have.

say.said: Magari avessi più tempo!
say.en: If only I had more time!
